text:
Livewire 4.1 introduced notable modifications to the behavior of `wire:model` modifiers, primarily altering how client-side state synchronizes and how events are listened for. These updates require developers to adjust their `wire:model` implementations to ensure expected functionality for data binding and event handling [1][2].

## Revised Behavior of `.blur` and `.change` Modifiers
A significant change in Livewire 4.1 concerns the `.blur` and `.change` modifiers. In Livewire 3, these modifiers exclusively dictated when a network request was dispatched, while the client-side state of the associated property updated immediately as a user typed. However, in **Livewire 4.1, these modifiers now control both the timing of client-side state synchronization and the network request itself** [1][3][2].

To revert to the Livewire 3 behavior, where the client-side state updates in real-time even when using `.blur` or `.change`, developers must now explicitly prepend the `.live` modifier. For instance, `wire:model.live.blur` will ensure immediate client-side updates while deferring the network request until the input loses focus [1][3].

This shift initially led to an issue in Livewire v4.1.0 where inputs with `wire:model.blur` or `wire:model.change` failed to send their values upon form submission via the Enter key. This could result in data loss if the `.enter` modifier was not also explicitly included. This bug was subsequently **addressed and fixed in Livewire v4.1.1** [4].

## Default Event Listening and the `.deep` Modifier
Livewire 4.1 also modified `wire:model`'s default event listening behavior. **`wire:model` now, by default, only responds to events that originate directly from the element it is bound to**, mirroring the functionality previously provided by the `.self` modifier [1]. To enable `wire:model` to capture events that bubble up from child elements within a component, developers must now **explicitly use the `.deep` modifier** [1][5]. This change prevents unintended interactions, such as a `wire:model` on a container element reacting to events from internal form inputs.

## Other Noteworthy Changes and Considerations
Beyond these core adjustments, Livewire 4.1 introduced other points for developer consideration. In v4.1.0, the **order of modifiers became temporarily significant**, particularly for `.live` and `.self`. For example, `wire:model.live.self` allowed changes to propagate to a parent component, while `wire:model.self.live` did not. This modifier order issue has since been fixed in the main branch [6]. Furthermore, the `.blur` modifier was found to have never functioned as intended on `#[Modelable]` components and has consequently been **removed from relevant documentation**, with event-based modifiers like `.blur` instead targeting DOM events within the child component itself [7][8].

## Conclusion
Livewire 4.1 significantly refined `wire:model` modifier functionality, primarily by extending the roles of `.blur` and `.change` to include client-side state synchronization. Developers must now adapt by using the `.live` modifier to preserve real-time client-side updates and employing the `.deep` modifier to capture events from child elements. These changes aim to provide more granular control over data flow and event propagation within Livewire applications.

sources.title: Upgrade Guide | Laravel Livewire
claims: In Livewire v4.1, modifiers like `.blur` and `.change` now control when client-side state syncs, not just network timing.
If using `.blur` or `.change` modifiers in Livewire v4.1 and desiring the previous behavior, add `.live` before them (e.g., `wire:model.live.blur`).
In Livewire v4, `wire:model` now only listens for events originating directly on the element itself, equivalent to the `.self` modifier behavior.
To capture events from child elements with `wire:model` in Livewire v4, add the `.deep` modifier (e.g., `wire:model.deep`).
In Livewire v4, modifiers like `.blur` and `.change` now control when client-side state syncs, in addition to controlling when network requests are sent.
To retain the previous behavior of `.blur` or `.change` modifiers in Livewire v4, add `.live` before the modifier (e.g., `wire:model.live.blur`).
The `wire:model.lazy` modifier in Livewire v4 continues to work as it did in v3.
In Livewire v4, `wire:model` expressions now support bracket notation for accessing nested properties, interpreting square brackets (`[` and `]`) as property accessors.

sources.title: livewire/docs/upgrading.md at 4.x · livewire/livewire · GitHub
claims: In Livewire v4.1, modifiers like .blur and .change now control when client-side state syncs, not just network timing.
To retain the previous behavior of .blur and .change modifiers in Livewire v4.1, users should add .live before them, e.g., wire:model.live.blur.
In Livewire v3, modifiers like .blur and .change only controlled when network requests were sent, while client-side state synced immediately.
In Livewire v4, .blur and .change modifiers control both client-side state sync timing and network request timing.
To achieve the v3 behavior of .blur and .change in Livewire v4, the .live modifier must be added before them (e.g., wire:model.live.blur).

sources.title: Livewire 3 to 4 Migration Guide: Upgrade in 30 Minutes
claims: In Livewire 3, wire:model.blur and wire:model.change controlled only when the network request fired, while client-side $wire.property synced in real-time.
In Livewire 4, wire:model.blur and wire:model.change control when client state syncs as well as when the network request fires.
To preserve the old Livewire 3 behavior where client state synced live even with .blur or .change modifiers, the .live modifier must be added in Livewire 4 (e.g., wire:model.live.blur).
The plain .blur modifier without .live in Livewire 4 defers both client state sync and the network request until the user leaves the field.
For validation-as-you-type patterns, wire:model.live.debounce.300ms is often recommended in Livewire 4.

sources.title: v4.1 wire:model.blur not sending input's values w/ payload when Enter pressed in same input to submit form · livewire/livewire · Discussion #9858 · GitHub
claims: In Livewire v4.1.0, the `wire:model.blur` modifier does not send the input's value in the event payload when the Enter key is pressed to submit a form, unless the `.enter` modifier is also explicitly added.
This behavior in Livewire v4.1.0 can lead to lost user-inputted data if the `.enter` modifier is forgotten on `.blur` or `.change` inputs.
The `wire:model.live.blur` modifier in Livewire v4.1.0 updates the ephemeral data on every keystroke, which is equivalent to the pre-v4.1 behavior of `wire:model.blur`.
A fix for the issue where `wire:model.blur` did not send input values on Enter key press was submitted via PR #9873 and confirmed to work in v4.1.1.

sources.title: wire:model | Laravel Livewire
claims: The `.live` modifier for `wire:model` enables server updates as a user types.
By default, `wire:model.live` has a 150-millisecond debounce.
The debounce time for `wire:model.live` can be customized using `.debounce.Xms` (e.g., `wire:model.live.debounce.250ms="title"`).
The `.blur` modifier for `wire:model` delays syncing until the user clicks away from the input.
The `.change` modifier for `wire:model` triggers on the change event, useful for select elements.
The `.enter` modifier for `wire:model` syncs when the user presses the Enter key.
The `.deep` modifier for `wire:model` allows it to respond to events bubbling up from child elements.
The `.renderless` modifier for `wire:model` sends a live model update to the server without re-rendering the component.
Nested properties can be accessed using dot notation (e.g., `wire:model="address.city"`) or bracket notation (e.g., `wire:model="address['city']"`).
Array elements can be accessed using dot notation (e.g., `wire:model="items.0.name"`) or bracket notation (e.g., `wire:model="items[0].name"`).

sources.title: Order of modifiers in wire:model (v4.1+) · livewire/livewire · Discussion #9878 · GitHub
claims: In Livewire version 4.1.0, the order of modifiers in wire:model is important when using .live and .self modifiers.
When wire:model is set to .live.self, changes in the child component bubble up to the parent.
When wire:model is set to .self.live, changes do not bubble up to the parent.
A fix for the wire:model modifier order issue was merged into the main branch of Livewire via commit 2cda6d74.
In Livewire v4.x, wire:model should ignore child events by default, making the .self modifier unnecessary.

sources.title: wire:model modifiers bug with Modelable components · livewire/livewire · Discussion #9952 · GitHub
claims: Livewire version v4.1.3 has a bug with wire:model modifiers on Modelable components.
The .blur modifier does not work as expected on modelable Livewire components.
The .live.blur modifier updates local state on every input event but does not send a network request on blur.
The .blur.live modifier updates local state and sends a network request on every input event.
A fix for the wire:model modifier bug on modelable components was submitted in PR #9993.
The .blur modifier was removed from the documentation for modelable components because it never worked.

sources.title: Modelable | Laravel Livewire
claims: The `#[Modelable]` attribute in Livewire allows a property in a child component to be bound from a parent component using `wire:model`.
Without `#[Modelable]`, manual handling of two-way communication between parent and child components is required.
The parent can use `wire:model` modifiers like `.live`, `.debounce.500ms`, and `.live.throttle.500ms` for timing and network control with modelable components.
Event-based modifiers like `.blur`, `.change`, and `.enter` on `wire:model` control DOM events on specific elements within the child component, not reactive component bindings.
Livewire currently supports only one `#[Modelable]` attribute per component.
